    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.

        polls |= set(re.findall(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\([^;]*?,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))
        for fn in polls:
            m = re.search(r'\b(?:static\s+)?\w[\w\s\*]*?\b'+re.escape(fn)+r'\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{', txt)
            if not m: continue

            while j < len(txt):

                elif txt[j]=='}':

                    if depth==0: break

            while j < len(txt):

root = '.'
out = subprocess.run(['find','drivers','net','-name','*.c'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
napi_hits = []
tasklet_hits = []
for path in out:
    try:
        txt = open(path, errors='ignore').read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    if 'netif_napi_add' in txt or 'napi_schedule' in txt:
        # find NAPI poll function names
        polls = set(re.findall(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\([^;]*?,\s*&?[\w\-]+,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))
        polls |= set(re.findall(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\([^;]*?,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))
        for fn in polls:
            m = re.search(r'\b(?:static\s+)?\w[\w\s\*]*?\b'+re.escape(fn)+r'\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{', txt)
            if not m: continue
            start = m.start()
            # extract body approx: until matching close brace
            depth = 0; i = txt.find('{', m.start())
            j = i
            while j < len(txt):
                if txt[j]=='{': depth+=1
                elif txt[j]=='}':
                    depth-=1
                    if depth==0: break
                j+=1
            body = txt[i:j]
            if re.search(r'spin_lock\(', body) and 'spin_lock_bh' not in body and 'local_bh_disable' not in body:
                lines = txt[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
                plain = re.findall(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\(&?[\w\->\.]+(?:\[[^\]]*\])?(?:,\s*\w+)?\)', body)
                napi_hits.append((path, lines, fn, plain[:4]))
    if 'tasklet_schedule' in txt or 'tasklet_init' in txt or 'tasklet_setup' in txt:
        fns = set(re.findall(r'tasklet_(?:init|setup)\s*\([^;]*?,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))

            m = re.search(r'\b(?:static\s+)?\w[\w\s\*]*?\b'+re.escape(fn)+r'\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{', txt)
            if not m: continue
            i = txt.find('{', m.start()); depth=0; j=i
            while j < len(txt):
                if txt[j]=='{': depth+=1
                elif txt[j]=='}':
                    depth-=1
                    if depth==0: break
                j+=1
            body = txt[i:j]
            if re.search(r'spin_lock\(', body):
                lines = txt[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
                plain = re.findall(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\(&?[\w\->\.]+(?:\[[^\]]*\])?(?:,\s*\w+)?\)', body)
                tasklet_hits.append((path, lines, fn, plain[:4]))

print("=== NAPI polls with plain spin_lock (no bh in body) ===")
for h in sorted(napi_hits):
    print(h)
print()
print("=== Tasklet callbacks containing spin_lock (any) ===")

import re, os, subprocess

root = 'drivers/net'
# find NAPI poll registrations
out = subprocess.run(['grep','-rn','--include=*.c','netif_napi_add','drivers/','net/'],capture_output=True,text=True)
napi_polls = []
for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
    m = re.search(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*&?([\w\>\.\-\>]+)\s*,\s*(\w+)\s*,', line)
    if m:
        path, ln = line.split(':',2)[0], line.split(':',2)[1]
        napi_polls.append((path, ln, m.group(2)))
print("NAPI poll fns:", len(napi_polls))
# now find those poll function bodies containing plain spin_lock(
from collections import defaultdict
bysig = defaultdict(list)
for path, ln, fn in napi_polls:
    byfn = subprocess.run(['grep','-n', r'^static.*\b'+fn+r'\b', path], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    m = re.search(r'^(\d+):', byfn)
    if m:
        start = int(m.group(1))
        # read function body until closing brace at col 0
        body = []
        with open(path, errors='ignore') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
        depth = 0; started=False
        for i in range(start-1, min(start+250, len(lines))):
            l = lines[i]
            body.append(l)
            depth += l.count('{') - l.count('}')
            if '{' in l: started=True
            if started and depth<=0:
                break
        text=''.join(body)
        if re.search(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(', text) and 'spin_lock_bh' not in text and 'spin_lock_irqsave' not in text:
            bysig[path].append((ln, fn, start))
for path, entries in sorted(bysig.items()):
    for ln, fn, start in entries:
        print(path, 'regline', ln, 'fn', fn, 'defline', start)
EOF

input.command:
T="$TMPDIR"; while IFS=$'\t' read -r f cb; do
  def=$(grep -n "^\(static \)\?\(void \|[a-zA-Z_]* \)\?$cb(" $f 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$def" ] && def=$(grep -n "$cb(struct\|$cb(unsigned" $f 2>/dev/null | grep -v tasklet_init | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$def" ] && continue
  end=$((def+80))
  body=$(sed -n "${def},${end}p" $f)
  # stop at closing brace of function heuristically: find first line that is "}"
  n=$(echo "$body" | grep -n "^}" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -n "$n" ] && end=$((def+n))
  hasplain=$(sed -n "${def},${end}p" $f | grep -c 'spin_lock(&\|spin_lock((\|_spin_lock(&')
  hasbh=$(sed -n "${def},${end}p" $f | grep -c 'spin_lock_bh\|spin_lock_irqsave\|spin_lock_irq(')
  if [ "$hasplain" -gt 0 ]; then echo -e "$f\t$cb\t$def\t$end\tplain=$hasplain bh=$hasbh"; fi
done < $T/tasklet_cbs.tsv > $T/tasklet_plain_cb.txt; wc -l < $T/tasklet_plain_cb.txt; cat $T/tasklet_plain_cb.txt

{

  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

From i011's candidate about ath9k: sc_pcu_lock taken plain spin_lock inside ath9k_tasklet (softirq side) but process side uses spin_lock_bh — safe for branch 1. But wait — for the tasklet branch, the direction matters: the dangerous direction is a plain process-context holder vs a softirq-side acquirer. In ath9k, the tasklet-side takes plain spin_lock on sc_pcu_lock and the process side uses spin_lock_bh... Actually wait: if the process side uses spin_lock_bh, BH is disabled so the tasklet cannot run on that CPU — safe. The tasklet-side plain acquisition is fine because a tasklet can't be interrupted by another tasklet on the same CPU (tasklets are serialized per-CPU — well, normal tasklets of the same type; actually a tasklet running cannot be preempted by another tasklet since TASKLET_STATE_RUN prevents re-entry of the same tasklet, but other softirqs could run? Within a softirq, another softirq can interrupt... Actually a softirq running on a CPU disables bottom halves? No — softirqs run with BH enabled (in ksoftirqd context BH enabled; in interrupt-exit context, softirqs run with local_bh_disable? Let me think: when do_softirq runs from irq exit, it runs with preemption/BH disabled? __do_softirq runs with local_bh_disable (softirq count incremented). So within a tasklet, BH is effectively disabled (softirq context implies BH disabled). So plain spin_lock in a tasklet is fine w.r.t. other tasklets. The dangerous direction is process-context plain holder vs softirq acquirer.)

So the pattern to find: lock object where
1. There's a softirq-side acquisition in a tasklet callback / NAPI poll / NET_RX/TX softirq callback (plain or _bh — doesn't matter; plain on softirq side is fine, but the lock must be shared)
2. There's a process-context acquisition with plain spin_lock (no _bh, no irqsave, no surrounding local_bh_disable)

  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

import re, os, json

TMP = os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp")
cbs = json.load(open(TMP + "/tasklet_cbs.json"))
tlock = json.load(open(TMP + "/tasklet_locks.json"))

# Build map: for each tasklet callback lock, check whether the same lock expression
# is acquired with plain spin_lock( elsewhere in the same file
report = []
for r in tlock:
    f = r["file"]
    src = open(f, errors="ignore").read()
    for lk, full in r["locks"]:
        # plain spin_lock( with this lock
        pat = re.compile(r"spin_lock\s*\(\s*&?" + re.escape(lk))
        plain_sites = [src.count("\n", 0, m.start())+1 for m in pat.finditer(src)]
        # exclude sites inside tasklet body
        body_start = r["def_line"]
        # filter: keep only lines NOT between def_line and def_line+60
        plain_out = [p for p in plain_sites if not (body_start <= p <= body_start+80)]
        if plain_out:
            report.append({"file": f, "cb": r["cb"], "lock": lk, "plain_sites": plain_out[:10], "n": len(plain_out)})

json.dump(report, open(TMP + "/tasklet_plain_share.json", "w"), indent=1)
print(len(report), "shared-lock candidates")
for r in report:
    print(f'{r["file"]:70s} {r["cb"]:35s} {r["lock"]:30s} plain@{r["plain_sites"]} ({r["n"]})')
PYEOF

PATH: drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/fs_enet/fs_enet-main.c 770 779
REASON: TASKLET/NAPI-softirq analogue of the seed's missing-BH-disable invariant in snapshot s01. LOCK OBJECT: struct fs_enet_private.tx_lock (spin_lock_init at drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/fs_enet/fs_enet-main.c:1003). SOFTIRQ SIDE (NAPI poll, NET_RX softirq via napi_schedule): fs_enet_interrupt (hardirq, request_irq at fs_enet-main.c:744) -> napi_schedule_prep (343) / __napi_schedule(&fep->napi) (351) -> fs_enet_napi (NAPI poll fn, def line 85, netif_napi_add_weight at 1020) takes the SAME fep->tx_lock with plain spin_lock at line 98 and completes TX descriptors under it while looping up to budget; the .ndo_tx_timeout watchdog path is excluded per branch scope, but the NAPI chain is in-scope. PROCESS SIDE (holder, missing BH disable): fs_enet_close (.ndo_stop, netdev_ops at fs_enet-main.c:896) runs in process context (ifconfig down / netlink) and acquires the SAME fep->tx_lock with plain spin_lock at line 777 (inside fs_enet_close, def line 765) inside spin_lock_irqsave(&fep->lock) (776) - the outer irqsave disables hard IRQs but NOT bottom halves. MISSING GUARANTEE: zero spin_lock_bh/local_bh_disable on tx_lock anywhere in the file (only plain 98/523/777 and spin_lock_init 1003); a NET_RX softirq executing fs_enet_napi on the same CPU while the close path holds tx_lock spins forever because the preempted holder (process context, only preemption+IRQs disabled) can never resume -> softirq soft-lockup, watchdog/RCU stall, device stall DoS - exactly the ks7010 seed shape generalized to the NAPI side. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: (a) fs_enet_close calls napi_disable(&fep->napi) at line 772 BEFORE taking tx_lock, which waits out an in-flight NAPI poll - but the residual window remains: free_irq happens only at line 781 AFTER the lock section, so fs_enet_interrupt can still call __napi_schedule during the lock section and the newly scheduled NAPI poll (softirq, e.g. via ksoftirqd or local_bh_enable elsewhere) runs against the plain holder; (b) the interrupt handler itself (317-355) takes only fep->lock under spin_lock_irqsave, and napi_schedule_prep/__napi_schedule in hardirq marks NAPI_STATE_SCHED so the poll runs only after the current close-context returns - the strongest narrowing; the deadlock is therefore a residual-window hypothesis (medium, not high confidence). SECONDARY same-lock site in scope: fs_enet_start_xmit (.ndo_start_xmit at 897) takes the same plain tx_lock at 523 - this is the xmit-softirq path already covered by the xmit branch, referenced only as evidence the lock is softirq-shared. Static source analysis only; no runtime reproducer or lockdep run (tree lacks .config for standalone build).

PATH: drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/fs_enet/fs_enet-main.c 763 778
REASON: fep->tx_lock is shared between NET_RX softirq and process context. Softirq side: NAPI poll fs_enet_napi (def line 86, registered via netif_napi_add at line 1033, scheduled from hardirq fs_enet_interrupt, request_irq line 742, napi_schedule_prep line 344 / __napi_schedule line 352) takes the lock with plain spin_lock(&fep->tx_lock) at line 99 and holds it to line 188. Process side: fs_enet_close (lines 763-778) acquires the same lock with plain spin_lock(&fep->tx_lock) at line 775, nested inside spin_lock_irqsave(&fep->lock, flags) at line 774; irqsave on the outer fep->lock disables interrupts but NOT bottom halves, so a fs_enet_napi poll running on the same CPU spins forever against the preempted close() holder (soft lockup/RCU stall). The file contains zero spin_lock_bh/local_bh_disable acquisitions of tx_lock (grep verified: only plain and irqsave variants), including the xmit site at line 524, confirming the missing-BH-disable discipline. Counterevidence narrowing the window: napi_disable(&fep->napi) at line 770 and netif_stop_queue at 768 run before the plain lock, so only a poll already past napi_schedule_prep (or an interrupt between 770 and 774 racing on the shared IRQ) can contend; hence medium, not high. Matches the confirmed bug shape in sibling snapshots (facts f029/f031/f033).

PATH: drivers/net/ethernet/altera/altera_tse_main.c 1284 1287
REASON: priv->tx_lock is shared between NET_RX softirq and process context. Softirq side: NAPI poll tse_poll (def line 492, netif_napi_add line 1565, scheduled from hardirq altera_isr lines 532-543, request_irq lines 1207/1216 with IRQF_SHARED) calls tse_tx_complete, which takes plain spin_lock(&priv->tx_lock) at line 452. Process side: tse_shutdown (def line 1261) takes the same lock with plain spin_lock(&priv->tx_lock) at line 1286 after plain spin_lock(&priv->mac_cfg_lock) at 1285, with no BH disable anywhere in the sequence. The xmit path proves the required discipline is known: tse_start_xmit uses spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_lock) at line 568, so the shutdown-site plain acquisition is the deviation. Counterevidence narrowing the window to low confidence: napi_disable(&priv->napi) at line 1272, disable_rxirq/disable_txirq at 1276-1277, and free_irq at lines 1281-1282 all run before the plain lock at 1286, so only a poll already in flight (past __napi_schedule, before napi_disable waits it out) can contend with shutdown. Matches the low-confidence verdicts for this lock in sibling snapshots (facts f030/f031/f033).

PATH: drivers/net/ethernet/sun/cassini.c 232 258
REASON: cp->tx_lock[] is shared between NET_RX softirq and process/workqueue context. Softirq side: NAPI poll cas_poll (def line 2572, netif_napi_add line 5095, scheduled from interrupt handlers via spin_lock_irqsave(&cp->lock, flags) + napi_schedule(&cp->napi) at lines 2446/2497/2548, request_irq line 4272) reaches cas_tx_ringN, which takes plain spin_lock(&cp->tx_lock[ring]) at line 1850. Process/workqueue side: cas_reset_task (workqueue worker, def line 3993) calls cas_lock_all_save(cp, flags) at line 4020, and cas_close calls it at line 4317 after napi_disable at 4309; the helper (macro at 254-258) only does spin_lock_irqsave(&cp->lock, flags) then cas_lock_tx, and cas_lock_tx (lines 232-238) takes every tx_lock[i] with plain spin_lock_nested at line 237 -- IRQs are disabled but bottom halves are not, so an in-flight cas_poll/cas_tx_ringN on the same CPU can spin forever against the workqueue holder. The xmit path uses the correct discipline (spin_lock_irqsave(&cp->tx_lock[ring], flags) at line 2763), showing the plain nested acquisition in the helpers is the anomaly. Counterevidence: cas_reset_task calls netif_device_detach at 4019, which stops new xmits but does not quiesce a NAPI poll already scheduled; cas_close's napi_disable at 4309 narrows that window. Mirrors the confirmed cassini finding in sibling snapshot s06 (fact f013); medium confidence because the detach/napi_disable ordering shrinks the contending window.

#include <net/checksum.h>
#include <linux/printk.h>

#include "qlcnic.h"

#define QLCNIC_TX_ETHER_PKT		0x01
#define QLCNIC_TX_TCP_PKT		0x02
#define QLCNIC_TX_UDP_PKT		0x03
#define QLCNIC_TX_IP_PKT		0x04
#define QLCNIC_TX_TCP_LSO		0x05
#define QLCNIC_TX_TCP_LSO6		0x06
#define QLCNIC_TX_ENCAP_PKT		0x07
#define QLCNIC_TX_ENCAP_LSO		0x08
#define QLCNIC_TX_TCPV6_PKT		0x0b
#define QLCNIC_TX_UDPV6_PKT		0x0c

#define QLCNIC_FLAGS_VLAN_TAGGED	0x10
#define QLCNIC_FLAGS_VLAN_OOB		0x40

#define qlcnic_set_tx_vlan_tci(cmd_desc, v)	\
	(cmd_desc)->vlan_TCI = cpu_to_le16(v);
#define qlcnic_set_cmd_desc_port(cmd_desc, var)	\
	((cmd_desc)->port_ctxid |= ((var) & 0x0F))
#define qlcnic_set_cmd_desc_ctxid(cmd_desc, var)	\
	((cmd_desc)->port_ctxid |= ((var) << 4 & 0xF0))

#define qlcnic_set_tx_port(_desc, _port) \
	((_desc)->port_ctxid = ((_port) & 0xf) | (((_port) << 4) & 0xf0))

#define qlcnic_set_tx_flags_opcode(_desc, _flags, _opcode) \
	((_desc)->flags_opcode |= \
	cpu_to_le16(((_flags) & 0x7f) | (((_opcode) & 0x3f) << 7)))

#define qlcnic_set_tx_frags_len(_desc, _frags, _len) \
	((_desc)->nfrags__length = \
	cpu_to_le32(((_frags) & 0xff) | (((_len) & 0xffffff) << 8)))

/* owner bits of status_desc */
#define STATUS_OWNER_HOST	(0x1ULL << 56)
#define STATUS_OWNER_PHANTOM	(0x2ULL << 56)

/* Status descriptor:
   0-3 port, 4-7 status, 8-11 type, 12-27 total_length
   28-43 reference_handle, 44-47 protocol, 48-52 pkt_offset
   53-55 desc_cnt, 56-57 owner, 58-63 opcode
 */
#define qlcnic_get_sts_port(sts_data)	\
	((sts_data) & 0x0F)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_status(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 4) & 0x0F)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_type(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 8) & 0x0F)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_totallength(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 12) & 0xFFFF)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_refhandle(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 28) & 0xFFFF)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_prot(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 44) & 0x0F)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_pkt_offset(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 48) & 0x1F)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_desc_cnt(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 53) & 0x7)
#define qlcnic_get_sts_opcode(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 58) & 0x03F)

#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_refhandle(sts_data) 	\
	((sts_data) & 0x07FFF)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_length(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 16) & 0x0FFFF)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_l2_hdr_offset(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 32) & 0x0FF)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_l4_hdr_offset(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 40) & 0x0FF)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_timestamp(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 48) & 0x1)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_type(sts_data)	\
	(((sts_data) >> 49) & 0x7)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_push_flag(sts_data)		\
	(((sts_data) >> 52) & 0x1)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_seq_number(sts_data)		\
	((sts_data) & 0x0FFFFFFFF)
#define qlcnic_get_lro_sts_mss(sts_data1)		\
	((sts_data1 >> 32) & 0x0FFFF)

#define qlcnic_83xx_get_lro_sts_mss(sts) ((sts) & 0xffff)

/* opcode field in status_desc */
#define QLCNIC_SYN_OFFLOAD	0x03
#define QLCNIC_RXPKT_DESC  	0x04
#define QLCNIC_OLD_RXPKT_DESC	0x3f
#define QLCNIC_RESPONSE_DESC	0x05
#define QLCNIC_LRO_DESC  	0x12

#define QLCNIC_TCP_HDR_SIZE		20
#define QLCNIC_TCP_TS_OPTION_SIZE	12
#define QLCNIC_FETCH_RING_ID(handle)	((handle) >> 63)
#define QLCNIC_DESC_OWNER_FW		cpu_to_le64(STATUS_OWNER_PHANTOM)

#define QLCNIC_TCP_TS_HDR_SIZE (QLCNIC_TCP_HDR_SIZE + QLCNIC_TCP_TS_OPTION_SIZE)

/* for status field in status_desc */
#define STATUS_CKSUM_LOOP	0
#define STATUS_CKSUM_OK		2

#define qlcnic_83xx_pktln(sts)		((sts >> 32) & 0x3FFF)
#define qlcnic_83xx_hndl(sts)		((sts >> 48) & 0x7FFF)
#define qlcnic_83xx_csum_status(sts)	((sts >> 39) & 7)
#define qlcnic_83xx_opcode(sts)	((sts >> 42) & 0xF)
#define qlcnic_83xx_vlan_tag(sts)	(((sts) >> 48) & 0xFFFF)

{
  "hexsha": "058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018",
  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
index 9fb118e77a1f..f1d44e4955fc 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
@@ -395,9 +395,9 @@ int ks_wlan_hw_tx(struct ks_wlan_private *priv, void *p, unsigned long size,
 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 	result = enqueue_txdev(priv, p, size, complete_handler, skb);
-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"
}

Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.

    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()

    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)

content.thinking:
Orinoco is safe — it uses irqsave or bh correctly. Interesting: hermes (PCI/PCMCIA) uses irqsave; ezusb uses bh. So the orinoco rx tasklet is protected.

Let me now look at other strong candidates. Let me check ath5k (ani_tasklet, rxtq, txtq, beacontq), ath9k htc (rx_tasklet, tx_failed_tasklet), carl9170 usb_tasklet, ipw2100/ipw2200 irq_tasklet, b43legacy isr_tasklet and txtask, brcmsmac tasklet (brcms_dpc), rtl8188eu/rtl8192e/rtl8712/rtl8723bs, wlan-ng, mt76, qtnfmac, rt2x00, rtlwifi, zd1211rw.

The ks7010-like shape: process-context code with plain spin_lock sharing a lock with a tasklet callback.

Let me write a script to check for each tasklet callback body what locks they take, and then see if those locks are also taken with plain spin_lock from process context.

Actually a more efficient approach: for each driver with tasklets, dump the tasklet callback function body and grep for spin_lock (without _bh/_irq). Then check the lock names against plain spin_lock users elsewhere.

Let me start with a targeted automated scan: find all tasklet_init calls and callback names, extract each callback's locks.

print(f"total tasklet_init sites: {len(paths)}")
for l in paths:

import re,os,subprocess
root='.'
# Step 1: collect files with tasklet or napi usage

pat_napi=re.compile(r'\b(netif_napi_add|netif_napi_add_weight|napi_schedule|__napi_schedule)\b')
res=subprocess.run(['grep','-rl','-E','tasklet_schedule|tasklet_hi_schedule|tasklet_setup|tasklet_init|DECLARE_TASKLET','drivers/','net/','kernel/','mm/','block/','crypto/','fs/','sound/'],capture_output=True,text=True)
tasklet_files=set(res.stdout.split())
res2=subprocess.run(['grep','-rl','-E','netif_napi_add|netif_napi_add_weight','drivers/','net/'],capture_output=True,text=True)
napi_files=set(res2.stdout.split())
allf=sorted(tasklet_files|napi_files)
print('tasklet files:',len(tasklet_files),'napi files:',len(napi_files))
plain={}; bh={}
for f in allf:
    try:
        lines=open(f,errors='ignore').read().split('\n')
    except: continue
    p=sum(1 for l in lines if re.search(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(',l))
    b=sum(1 for l in lines if re.search(r'\bspin_lock_(bh|irq|irqsave|irqrestore|nested)\b',l) or re.search(r'\bspin_lock_bh\s*\(',l))
    if p>0:
        plain[f]=(p,b)
top=sorted(plain.items(),key=lambda kv:-kv[1][0])
for f,(p,b) in top[:60]:
    tag='T' if f in tasklet_files else '-'
    tag+='N' if f in napi_files else '-'
    print(f'{tag} {p:3d} plain, {b:3d} typed  {f}')

import re, os, json, sys

TMP = os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp")
cbs = json.load(open(TMP + "/tasklet_cbs.json"))

results = []
for f, funcs in cbs.items():
    if not f.endswith(".c"):
        continue
    try:
        src = open(f, errors="ignore").read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    lines = src.split("\n")
    for fn in funcs:
        # find function definition (best effort)
        for i, l in enumerate(lines):
            m = re.match(r"^(?:static\s+)?(?:void|int|irqreturn_t|unsigned long|long)\s+" + re.escape(fn) + r"\s*\(", l)
            if m:
                # capture function body with brace matching
                depth = 0; started = False; body = []
                for j in range(i, min(i+400, len(lines))):
                    body.append((j+1, lines[j]))
                    depth += lines[j].count("{") - lines[j].count("}")
                    if "{" in lines[j]:
                        started = True
                    if started and depth == 0:
                        break
                # locks taken in tasklet body
                locks = set()
                for ln, bl in body:
                    for mm in re.finditer(r"spin_lock(?:_irqsave|_irq|_bh)?\s*\(\s*&?([A-Za-z_0-9>\.\-]+)", bl):
                        locks.add((mm.group(1), mm.group(0)))
                if locks:
                    results.append({"file": f, "cb": fn, "def_line": i+1, "locks": sorted(locks)})
                break

json.dump(results, open(TMP + "/tasklet_locks.json", "w"), indent=1)
print(len(results), "tasklet callbacks taking spinlocks")
for r in results[:200]:
    print(r["file"], r["cb"], "line", r["def_line"], [x[0] for x in r["locks"]])

import re, os, json

TMP = os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp")
cbs = json.load(open(TMP + "/tasklet_cbs.json"))
tlock = json.load(open(TMP + "/tasklet_locks.json"))

# Build map: for each tasklet callback lock, check whether the same lock expression
# is acquired with plain spin_lock( elsewhere in the same file
report = []
for r in tlock:
    f = r["file"]
    src = open(f, errors="ignore").read()
    for lk, full in r["locks"]:
        # plain spin_lock( with this lock
        pat = re.compile(r"spin_lock\s*\(\s*&?" + re.escape(lk))
        plain_sites = [src.count("\n", 0, m.start())+1 for m in pat.finditer(src)]
        # exclude sites inside tasklet body
        body_start = r["def_line"]
        # filter: keep only lines NOT between def_line and def_line+60
        plain_out = [p for p in plain_sites if not (body_start <= p <= body_start+80)]
        if plain_out:
            report.append({"file": f, "cb": r["cb"], "lock": lk, "plain_sites": plain_out[:10], "n": len(plain_out)})

json.dump(report, open(TMP + "/tasklet_plain_share.json", "w"), indent=1)
print(len(report), "shared-lock candidates")
for r in report:
    print(f'{r["file"]:70s} {r["cb"]:35s} {r["lock"]:30s} plain@{r["plain_sites"]} ({r["n"]})')

napi_hits = []
tasklet_hits = []
for path in out:
    try:
        txt = open(path, errors='ignore').read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    if 'netif_napi_add' in txt or 'napi_schedule' in txt:
        # find NAPI poll function names
        polls = set(re.findall(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\([^;]*?,\s*&?[\w\-]+,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))
        polls |= set(re.findall(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\([^;]*?,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))
        for fn in polls:
            m = re.search(r'\b(?:static\s+)?\w[\w\s\*]*?\b'+re.escape(fn)+r'\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{', txt)
            if not m: continue
            start = m.start()
            # extract body approx: until matching close brace
            depth = 0; i = txt.find('{', m.start())
            j = i
            while j < len(txt):
                if txt[j]=='{': depth+=1
                elif txt[j]=='}':
                    depth-=1
                    if depth==0: break
                j+=1
            body = txt[i:j]
            if re.search(r'spin_lock\(', body) and 'spin_lock_bh' not in body and 'local_bh_disable' not in body:
                lines = txt[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
                plain = re.findall(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\(&?[\w\->\.]+(?:\[[^\]]*\])?(?:,\s*\w+)?\)', body)
                napi_hits.append((path, lines, fn, plain[:4]))
    if 'tasklet_schedule' in txt or 'tasklet_init' in txt or 'tasklet_setup' in txt:
        fns = set(re.findall(r'tasklet_(?:init|setup)\s*\([^;]*?,\s*(\w+)\s*,', txt))
        for fn in fns:
            m = re.search(r'\b(?:static\s+)?\w[\w\s\*]*?\b'+re.escape(fn)+r'\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{', txt)
            if not m: continue
            i = txt.find('{', m.start()); depth=0; j=i
            while j < len(txt):
                if txt[j]=='{': depth+=1
                elif txt[j]=='}':
                    depth-=1
                    if depth==0: break
                j+=1
            body = txt[i:j]
            if re.search(r'spin_lock\(', body):
                lines = txt[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
                plain = re.findall(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\(&?[\w\->\.]+(?:\[[^\]]*\])?(?:,\s*\w+)?\)', body)
                tasklet_hits.append((path, lines, fn, plain[:4]))

print("=== NAPI polls with plain spin_lock (no bh in body) ===")

    print(h)
print()
print("=== Tasklet callbacks containing spin_lock (any) ===")
for h in sorted(tasklet_hits):

def find_def(text, fname):
    # find "static ... fname(...)" up to matching closing brace at col 0
    pat = re.compile(r'^[^\n]*?\b' + re.escape(fname) + r'\s*\(', re.M)
    for m in pat.finditer(text):
        start = m.start()
        # take from start of line
        linestart = text.rfind('\n', 0, start)+1
        # find opening brace after
        b = text.find('{', m.end())
        if b == -1: continue
        # ensure no ';' between signature end and '{' (prototype)
        if ';' in text[m.end():b]:
            continue
        # match braces
        depth=0; i=b
        while i < len(text):
            if text[i]=='{': depth+=1
            elif text[i]=='}':
                depth-=1
                if depth==0: break
            i+=1
        return linestart, i+1
    return None

for f in files:

    lines = text.split('\n')

        if not r: continue
        s,e = r
        body = text[s:e]
        # plain spin_lock in body
        locks = set(re.findall(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*&([\w>\.\[\]~-]+)', body))
        if not locks: continue

        defline = text[:s].count('\n')+1
        for lk in locks:

            for mm in re.finditer(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*&' + re.escape(lk), text):

            bh = len(re.findall(r'spin_lock_bh\s*\(\s*&' + re.escape(lk), text))
            irq = len(re.findall(r'spin_lock_irq\w*\s*\(\s*&' + re.escape(lk), text))
            print(f"{f}\tcallback={cb}:{defline}\tlock={lk}\tplain_in_cb\tother_plain_sites={sites}\tbh={bh}\tirq={irq}")

def find_def(text, fname):
    pat = re.compile(r'^[^\n]*?\b' + re.escape(fname) + r'\s*\(', re.M)
    for m in pat.finditer(text):
        start = m.start()
        linestart = text.rfind('\n', 0, start)+1
        b = text.find('{', m.end())
        if b == -1: continue
        if ';' in text[m.end():b]: continue
        depth=0; i=b
        while i < len(text):
            if text[i]=='{': depth+=1
            elif text[i]=='}':
                depth-=1
                if depth==0: break
            i+=1
        return linestart, i+1
    return None
for f in files:
    path = os.path.join(root, f)
    text = open(path, errors='replace').read()
    # netif_napi_add(dev, &x->napi, poll, weight)
    for m in re.finditer(r'netif_napi_add\s*\(([^;]*?)\);', text, re.S):
        args = m.group(1)
        parts = [a.strip() for a in args.split(',')]
        # poll fn is typically 3rd arg; also match netif_napi_add(dev, napi, fn)
        cand = None
        for p in parts:
            if re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z_]\w*$', p) and not p in ('NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT',) and not p.endswith('_WEIGHT'):
                # heuristic: identifier that has a def in this file
                if find_def(text, p):
                    cand = p
        if not cand: continue
        r = find_def(text, cand)
        if not r: continue
        s,e = r
        body = text[s:e]
        locks = set(re.findall(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*&([\w>\.\[\]~-]+)', body))
        if not locks: continue
        defline = text[:s].count('\n')+1
        for lk in sorted(locks):
            plain = [text[:mm.start()].count('\n')+1 for mm in re.finditer(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*&' + re.escape(lk), text)]
            bh = [text[:mm.start()].count('\n')+1 for mm in re.finditer(r'spin_lock_bh\s*\(\s*&' + re.escape(lk), text)]
            print(f"{f}\tpoll={cand}:{defline}\tlock={lk}\tplain={plain}\tbh={bh}")

{
  "hexsha": "058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018",
  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
index 9fb118e77a1f..f1d44e4955fc 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
@@ -395,9 +395,9 @@ int ks_wlan_hw_tx(struct ks_wlan_private *priv, void *p, unsigned long size,
 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 	result = enqueue_txdev(priv, p, size, complete_handler, skb);
-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"
}

export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re, subprocess, os, json

TMP = os.environ.get("TMPDIR","/tmp")
root = "."
# parse tasklet registrations again
tasklet_re = re.compile(r'tasklet(?:_hi)?_init\s*\(\s*([^,]+),\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,')
setup_re  = re.compile(r'tasklet_setup\s*\(\s*([^,]+),\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\)')
declare_re = re.compile(r'DECLARE_TASKLET(?:_OLD)?\s*\(\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\)')
out = subprocess.run(["grep","-rn","--include=*.c","-e","tasklet_init(","-e","tasklet_setup(","-e","DECLARE_TASKLET"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
regs = []
for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
    f, ln, text = line.split(":", 2)
    for m in tasklet_re.finditer(text):
        regs.append((f, int(ln), m.group(2), m.group(1)))
    for m in setup_re.finditer(text):
        regs.append((f, int(ln), m.group(2), m.group(1)))
    for m in declare_re.finditer(text):
        regs.append((f, int(ln), m.group(2), m.group(1)))

lock_re = re.compile(r'(spin_lock|spin_unlock|spin_trylock|read_lock|write_lock)\s*\(\s*([^);]+?)\s*\)')

def func_body(fname, func):
    try:
        src = open(os.path.join(root, fname)).read()
    except OSError:
        return None
    # find definition: func at start of line-ish followed by ( ... ) {, tolerate newlines
    pat = re.compile(r'(^|\n)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_ \t\*&]*\b' + re.escape(func) + r'\s*\(')
    m = pat.search(src)
    if not m:
        return None
    i = m.start(1) if m.group(1) else m.start()
    # find first '{' after signature then match braces
    b = src.find('{', m.end()-1)
    if b < 0: return None
    depth = 0; j = b
    while j < len(src):
        c = src[j]
        if c == '{': depth += 1
        elif c == '}':
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
        j += 1
    return src[b:j+1], src[:b].count('\n')+1

results = []
for (fname, ln, cb, obj) in regs:
    got = func_body(fname, cb)
    if got is None:
        # callback defined in another file? search all
        continue
    body, defline = got
    locks = []
    for m in lock_re.finditer(body):
        kind, expr = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if any(k in kind for k in ('irq','_bh','bh')):
            continue  # only plain (safe-enough on the softirq side? actually we want ALL, but plain only for our defect)
        locks.append((kind, expr.strip()))
    if locks:
        results.append((fname, ln, cb, obj, locks))

print("tasklet callbacks containing plain spinlock acquisitions:", len(results))
for r in results:
    print(f"{r[0]}:{r[1]} cb={r[2]} obj={r[3]}")
    for k,e in r[4]:
        print(f"    {k}({e})")
with open(TMP+"/tasklet_plain_locks.txt","w") as fh:
    for r in results:
        fh.write(f"{r[0]}|{r[1]}|{r[2]}|{r[3]}\n")
        for k,e in r[4]:
            fh.write(f"  {k}({e})\n")

import re, subprocess, os

root="."
napi_re = re.compile(r'netif_napi_add\s*\(')
out = subprocess.run(["grep","-rn","--include=*.c","netif_napi_add("], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
regs=[]

    f, ln, text = line.split(":",2)
    regs.append((f,int(ln),text.strip()))
print("napi_add sites:", len(regs))
with open(os.environ.get("TMPDIR","/tmp")+"/napi_regs.txt","w") as fh:
    for f,ln,t in regs:
        fh.write(f"{f}:{ln} :: {t}\n")

# Extract poll function name: netif_napi_add(dev, &x->napi, poll_fn, weight) - poll is 3rd arg
# handle multiline
lock_re = re.compile(r'(spin_lock|spin_unlock|spin_trylock)\s*\(\s*([^);]+?)\s*\)')
def func_body(fname, func):
    try:
        src = open(os.path.join(root, fname)).read()
    except OSError:
        return None
    pat = re.compile(r'(^|\n)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_ \t\*&]*\b' + re.escape(func) + r'\s*\(')
    m = pat.search(src)
    if not m: return None
    b = src.find('{', m.end()-1)
    if b < 0: return None
    depth=0; j=b
    while j < len(src):
        c=src[j]
        if c=='{': depth+=1
        elif c=='}':
            depth-=1
            if depth==0: break
        j+=1
    return src[b:j+1]

results=[]
for f,ln,t in regs:
    # get full call possibly multiline: read from file a window
    try:
        src=open(os.path.join(root,f)).read().splitlines()
    except OSError: continue
    window = " ".join(src[ln-1:ln+4])
    # find args split by commas at top level
    m = re.search(r'netif_napi_add\s*\((.*)\)\s*;?', window)
    if not m: continue
    args_txt = m.group(1)
    # top-level split
    parts=[]; depth=0; cur=''
    for ch in args_txt:
        if ch=='(' : depth+=1
        if ch==')' : depth-=1
        if ch==',' and depth==0:
            parts.append(cur); cur=''
        else: cur+=ch
    parts.append(cur)
    if len(parts) < 4: continue
    poll = parts[2].strip()
    if not re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$', poll): continue
    got = func_body(f, poll)
    if got is None: continue
    body = got
    locks=[]
    for mm in lock_re.finditer(body):
        kind, expr = mm.group(1), mm.group(2)
        if any(k in kind for k in ('irq','_bh','bh')): continue
        locks.append((kind, expr.strip()))
    if locks:
        results.append((f,ln,poll,locks))
print("napi poll functions with plain spinlock:", len(results))
for r in results:
    print(f"{r[0]}:{r[1]} poll={r[2]}")
    for k,e in r[3]:
        print(f"    {k}({e})")

  "hexsha": "058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018",
  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c

--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c

 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);

-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"
}

```python
def func_body(src, name):
    # find definition: name(unsigned long ...) or name(struct tasklet_struct *...)
    # search for name followed by ( ... ) and then {
    idx = 0
    results = []
    pattern = re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\(')
    for m in pattern.finditer(src):
        # check it's a definition, not call: look for '{' before ';' after the closing paren
        i = m.end()
        depth = 1
        while i < len(src) and depth:
            if src[i]=='(': depth+=1
            elif src[i]==')': depth-=1
            i+=1
        # skip whitespace, find '{' before ';'
        j = i
        while j < len(src) and src[j] in ' \t\n':
            j+=1
        if j < len(src) and src[j]=='{':
            # extract body with brace counting
            k = j; d=0
            while k < len(src):
                if src[k]=='{': d+=1
                elif src[k]=='}':
                    d-=1
                    if d==0: break
                k+=1
            body = src[j:k+1]
            startline = src[:j].count('\n')+1
            results.append((startline, body))
    return results
```

  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)

    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>

    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 	result = enqueue_txdev(priv, p, size, complete_handler, skb);
-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"
}

import re, os, sys

root = os.getcwd()
tasklet_files = [l.strip() for l in open(os.environ['TMPDIR']+'/tasklet_files.txt') if l.strip()]

# collect tasklet_init(func) callback names per file
cb_re = re.compile(r'tasklet_init\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_0-9]+)')
hi_re = re.compile(r'tasklet_hi_schedule\s*\(\s*&?([A-Za-z_0-9>\.\-]+)')
sch_re = re.compile(r'tasklet_schedule\s*\(\s*&?([A-Za-z_0-9>\.\-]+)')

results = []
for f in tasklet_files:
    p = os.path.join(root, f)
    try:
        src = open(p, errors='replace').read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    cbs = set(cb_re.findall(src))
    if not cbs:
        continue
    # find callback body and check for spin_lock in the body (coarse: 80 lines after def)
    for cb in cbs:
        m = re.search(r'(?:^|\n)[A-Za-z_0-9 \*]+\b' + re.escape(cb) + r'\s*\(', src)
        if not m:
            continue
        start = m.start()
        body = src[m.end():m.end()+4000]
        # naive: find next function definition at col 0
        nxt = re.search(r'\n[A-Za-z_0-9 \*]+\([^;]*\)\s*\n\{', body)
        seg = body[:nxt.start()] if nxt else body[:3000]
        if re.search(r'spin_lock\s*\(', seg):
            results.append((f, cb, src[:m.end()].count('\n')+1))

for f, cb, line in results:
    print(f"{f}:{line}: tasklet cb {cb} takes spin_lock in body")
print(f"--- total {len(results)}")
PYEOF
python3 $TMPDIR/scan_tasklets.py

import re, os

root = os.getcwd()
tasklet_files = [l.strip() for l in open(os.environ['TMPDIR']+'/tasklet_files.txt') if l.strip()]
cb_re = re.compile(r'tasklet_init\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_0-9]+)')

# For each tasklet callback that takes a plain spin_lock, identify the lock expression
lock_re = re.compile(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*([^)]+?)\s*\)')

for f in tasklet_files:
    p = os.path.join(root, f)
    try:
        src = open(p, errors='replace').read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    for cb in set(cb_re.findall(src)):
        m = re.search(r'(?:^|\n)[A-Za-z_0-9 \*]+\b' + re.escape(cb) + r'\s*\(', src)
        if not m:
            continue
        body = src[m.end():m.end()+4000]
        nxt = re.search(r'\n[A-Za-z_0-9 \*]+\([^;]*\)\s*\n\{', body)
        seg = body[:nxt.start()] if nxt else body[:3000]
        locks = lock_re.findall(seg)
        if locks:
            # find whether the same lock is taken with _bh or _irqsave elsewhere in the same file
            for L in set(x.strip() for x in locks):
                bh = len(re.findall(r'spin_lock_bh\s*\(\s*' + re.escape(L) + r'\s*\)', src))
                irqs = len(re.findall(r'spin_lock_irqsave\s*\(\s*' + re.escape(L), src))
                plain = len(re.findall(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*' + re.escape(L) + r'\s*\)', src))
                print(f"{f}\t{cb}\tlock={L}\tplain={plain}\tbh={bh}\tirqsave={irqs}")
PYEOF
python3 $TMPDIR/scan_bh_perspective.py

import re, os

root = os.getcwd()
# gather files with netif_napi_add
out = os.popen("/usr/bin/rg -l 'netif_napi_add' --type c drivers net").read()
files = [l.strip() for l in out.splitlines() if l.strip()]

for f in files:
    p = os.path.join(root, f)
    try:
        src = open(p, errors='replace').read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    # extract poll function names from netif_napi_add(..., func, ...)
    for m in re.finditer(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\(', src):
        # parse args crudely: take up to matching paren, split by commas at depth 0
        i = m.end(); depth = 1; j = i
        while j < len(src) and depth:
            if src[j] == '(': depth += 1
            elif src[j] == ')': depth -= 1
            j += 1
        args = src[i:j-1]
        parts = re.split(r',(?![^()]*\))', args)
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            fn = parts[3].strip()
            fn = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z_0-9]', '', fn)
            if not fn:
                continue
            dm = re.search(r'(?:^|\n)[A-Za-z_0-9 \*]+\b' + re.escape(fn) + r'\s*\(', src)
            if not dm:
                continue
            body = src[dm.end():dm.end()+4000]
            nxt = re.search(r'\n[A-Za-z_0-9 \*]+\([^;]*\)\s*\n\{', body)
            seg = body[:nxt.start()] if nxt else body[:3000]
            locks = re.findall(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*([^)]+?)\s*\)', seg)
            if locks:
                line = src[:dm.end()].count('\n') + 1
                print(f"{f}:{line}: NAPI poll {fn} plain-locks {set(lock.strip() for lock in locks)}")
PYEOF

  "hexsha": "058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018",
  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
index 9fb118e77a1f..f1d44e4955fc 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
@@ -395,9 +395,9 @@ int ks_wlan_hw_tx(struct ks_wlan_private *priv, void *p, unsigned long size,
 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re, os, subprocess, json

# Inventory: files containing tasklet_init / DECLARE_TASKLET
out = subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/rg','-l','tasklet_init\(|DECLARE_TASKLET','-g','*.c','drivers/','net/','sound/'],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
out = sorted(set(f for f in out if not f.startswith(('tools/','Documentation/'))))
print("tasklet files:", len(out))

lockexpr = re.compile(r'spin_(?:un)?lock(?:_irqsave|_irqrestore|_irq|_bh|_nosync)?\s*\(\s*&?([^),]+)')
for f in out:
    src = open(f, errors='ignore').read()
    # spinlock fields declared in this file's structs
    locks = set(re.findall(r'struct spinlock\s+(\w+)|spinlock_t\s+(\w+)', src))
    locknames = {a or b for a,b in locks}
    if not locknames: continue
    exprs = lockexpr.findall(src)
    plain = {}
    for e in exprs:
        base = e.strip().split('.')[-1].split('->')[-1].strip()
        if base in locknames:
            plain.setdefault(base, []).append(e.strip())
    if plain:
        print(f, sorted(plain.keys()))
PYEOF

import re, subprocess, collections

out = subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/rg','-l','tasklet_init[,(]|DECLARE_TASKLET','-g','*.c','drivers/','net/','sound/'],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()

pair = re.compile(r'spin_(lock|unlock)(?:_irqsave|_irqrestore|_irq|_bh|_nosync)?\s*\(\s*&?\s*([A-Za-z_][\w]*(?:\s*(?:->|\.)\s*[A-Za-z_]\w*)*)')
results = {}
for f in out:
    src = open(f, errors='ignore').read()
    byname = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for m in pair.finditer(src):
        expr = m.group(2).replace(' ','')
        base = re.split(r'->|\.', expr)[-1]
        byname[base].add(m.group(0).rstrip('(.').strip())
    hits = [(b, sorted(s)) for b, s in byname.items() if len(s) > 1]
    if hits:
        results[f] = hits

for f, h in sorted(results.items()):
    print("==", f)
    for base, sfx in h:
        print("   ", base, "->", sfx)
print("TOTAL files with mixed suffixes:", len(results))
PYEOF

import re, subprocess, collections, os

out = subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/rg','-l','tasklet_init[,(]|DECLARE_TASKLET','-g','*.c','drivers/','net/','sound/'],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
pair = re.compile(r'spin_(lock|unlock)(?:_irqsave|_irqrestore|_irq|_bh|_nosync)?\s*\(\s*&?\s*([A-Za-z_][\w]*(?:\s*(?:->|\.)\s*[A-Za-z_]\w*)*)')

for f in out:
    src = open(f, errors='ignore').read()
    # find lock exprs taken BOTH with plain spin_lock AND with a stronger variant
    byname = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(list))
    for m in pair.finditer(src):
        expr = m.group(2).replace(' ','')
        base = re.split(r'->|\.', expr)[-1]
        m2 = re.match(r'spin_(lock|unlock)(.*)', m.group(0))
        suffix = m2.group(2).split('(')[0]
        line = src[:m.start()].count('\n') + 1
        byname[base][suffix or 'plain'].append(line)
    interesting = []
    for base, d in byname.items():
        if 'plain' in d and ('_bh' in d or '_irq' in d or '_irqsave' in d):
            interesting.append((base, {k:v for k,v in d.items()}))
    if interesting:
        for base, d in interesting:
            print(f"{f}: {base}: {dict(d)}")
PYEOF

{
  "hexsha": "058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018",
  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com

1. Enumerate tasklet users: files with `tasklet_init(` or `tasklet_setup(` in s10.
2. Enumerate NAPI: files with `netif_napi_add(` and `napi_schedule`.
3. For each candidate file, find lock objects used in the tasklet callback / NAPI poll body, then check if same lock is acquired with plain `spin_lock(` (not _bh/_irq/_irqsave) in a process-context function (workqueue work func, ioctl, open/close, cfg80211 ops, ethtool, etc.).

Note: delayed_work run from workqueue is process context... wait, branch2 covers timer_list/hrtimer/delayed_work callback bodies as the softirq side? Actually delayed_work callbacks run in process context (kworker), not softirq. Hmm, the branch2 description says "locks acquired inside timer_list, hrtimer, or delayed_work callback bodies (timer softirq context)". Actually delayed_work uses a timer to queue work, and the work runs in a worker (process context). But the branch statement treats it that way. Anyway for branch3, I need tasklet_schedule'd callbacks and NAPI poll functions and other NET_RX/NET_TX softirq callbacks.

Important: the softirq side (tasklet body or NAPI poll) taking plain spin_lock is fine per se; the defect is the process-context side taking plain spin_lock on a lock also acquired in softirq context. Both sides take plain spin_lock — process side must use spin_lock_bh.

import re, subprocess, os, json
RG="/usr/bin/rg"
# 1. tasklet callback map
tcb = {}
out = subprocess.run([RG,"-n","tasklet_init\(|tasklet_setup\(","drivers","net"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
for line in out.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r'([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)', line)
    if not m: continue
    f,ln,txt = m.group(1),int(m.group(2)),m.group(3)
    fn = re.findall(r'([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,?\s*(?:\(\w+\))?\s*,\s*$|,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,', txt)
    names = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*', txt)
    # tasklet_init(&x->t, callback, (unsigned long)x) — callback is 2nd identifier after comma
    # find tokens that look like function names: after first comma
    parts = txt.split(',')
    if len(parts)>=2:
        cb = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*', parts[1])
        if cb:
            tcb.setdefault(cb[0], []).append(f"{f}:{ln}")
print("tasklet callbacks:", len(tcb))
# 2. for each callback file, extract plain spin_lock usage
cands = {}
for cb, sites in tcb.items():
    f = sites[0].split(':')[0]
    if not f.endswith('.c'): continue
    try: src = open(f, errors='ignore').read()
    except: continue
    if 'spin_lock(' in src or re.search(r'spin_lock\s*\(', src):
        cands[cb] = (f, sites)
print("tasklet-callback files with plain spin_lock:", len(cands))
for cb,(f,sites) in sorted(cands.items()):
    print(f"{cb:35s} {sites[0]}")
json.dump({cb:list(v[1]) for cb,v in cands.items()}, open('/tmp/tcand.json','w'))
EOF
input.description: Map tasklet callbacks and filter files with plain spin_lock

  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

cd "$TMPDIR" && cat > i039/express.py <<'PY'
import subprocess, re, os
ROOT="/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s10"
def run(cmd):
    return subprocess.run(cmd,shell=True,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=ROOT).stdout

files = run("grep -rln --include=*.c 'tasklet_init' drivers net sound block").split()
report=[]
for f in files:
    src=open(os.path.join(ROOT,f),errors='ignore').read()
    lines=src.split('\n')
    # plain spin_lock lines
    plain=[]
    for i,l in enumerate(lines,1):
        if re.search(r'(?<![a-z_])spin_lock\s*\(', l) or 'spin_lock_nested' in l:
            plain.append(i)
    if not plain: continue
    cbs = re.findall(r'tasklet_init\s*\(\s*&?[\w\->\.]+,\s*(\w+)', src)
    cbs += re.findall(r'tasklet_setup\s*\(\s*&?[\w\->\.]+,\s*(\w+)', src)
    cbs += [m for m in re.findall(r'DECLARE_TASKLET\s*\(\s*\w+\s*,\s*(\w+)', src)]
    if not cbs: continue
    # extract body of each cb
    def body(name):
        m=re.search(r'\b\w[\w\s\*]*?\b'+re.escape(name)+r'\s*\(', src)
        if not m: return ""
        st=src.find('{', m.end())
        if st<0: return ""
        d=0
        for k in range(st,len(src)):
            if src[k]=='{':d+=1
            elif src[k]=='}':
                d-=1
                if d==0: return src[st:k+1]
        return ""
    cblocks={c:body(c) for c in set(cbs)}
    cb_plain_locks=set()
    for c,b in cblocks.items():
        for m in re.finditer(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\s*\(\s*([^;]+?)\s*\)', b):
            cb_plain_locks.add(m.group(1).strip().rstrip(',').split(',')[0])
    if not cb_plain_locks: continue
    # candidate lock names: base identifiers of cb plain locks
    base=set()
    for lk in cb_plain_locks:
        base |= set(re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*', lk))
    # plain sites in file whose lock expr shares base tokens with cb locks and are NOT inside any cb body
    hits=[]
    for ln in plain:
        expr=None
        for i in range(ln, 0, -1):
            m=re.search(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\s*\(\s*([^;]+?)\s*\)', lines[i-1])
            if m:
                expr=m.group(1); break
        if expr is None: continue
        # skip if inside a cb body line range
        inside=False
        for c,b in cblocks.items():
            # find start line of cb def
            m=re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(c)+r'\s*\(', src)
            if m:
                startline=src[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
                if startline<=ln<=startline+b.count('\n')+2:
                    inside=True;break
        if inside: continue
        toks=set(re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*', expr))
        if toks & base:
            hits.append((ln,expr))
    if hits:
        report.append((f,sorted(cb_plain_locks),hits))
for f,locks,hits in report:
    print(f)
    print("  cb plain locks:",sorted(locks))
    for ln,e in hits: print(f"   noncb plain: {ln}: {e}")
PY

  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock

    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
